740051102.text: Straightforward, huh? Well, that saves us time as well!

740051103.text: See, what did I tell you...

740050301.text: (The sound of rummaging comes from beyond the door...)

740050302.text: Uh, that was louder than Paimon thought it would be.

740050303.text: Uh... My paints... But they should be here...

740050401.text: Actually, we've said a lot so far, but what should we call you, again?

740050402.text: Mamere. My name is Mamere. I was painting here, but...

740050403.text: Ooh, so Melusines can paint too?

740050404.text: Yes... I do. Every day, in fact. Because painting the things that I want to brings me happiness.

740050405.text: Well, aren't you a painter, then?

740050406.text: I see. I'm not sure I understand what you mean, but I guess so.

740050408.text: #Anyway, let's help gather up the painting tools first, {NICKNAME}. Considering how short her hands are, Paimon's can't even imagine how she'd hold a brush...

740050409.text: But your hands are shorter than mine...

740050410.text: ...Thank you. It would take a long time for me to clean them up.

740050411.text: You help Mamere pick up the scattered painting tools...

740050412.text: Well, looks like we're more or less done! Good job, Paimon!

740050415.text: H—Hey, it's called a division of labor!

740050417.text: Speaking of which, what were those people actually trying to do?

740050418.text: Them? Hmm... They wanted to exchange Mora for the paintings in my hands.

740050419.text: Oh, so they wanted to— wait, then they were here to buy your art after all, weren't they?

740050420.text: Uh oh, wh—what do we do? Sounds like we had good intentions, but we ended up interrupting a business transaction you were having...

740050421.text: Business? I... don't think you could call it that. Don't both sides have to exchange things the other needs for it to be called "business"?

740050422.text: I don't need Mora... so that wasn't business.

740050423.text: You don't need Mora? Wait, you're not some sorta renowned painter, are you?

740050426.text: Renown? Does that mean that people know about you?

740050427.text: I guess I count then? Previously, a stranger claiming to be an art collector or something asked to exchange a large sum of Mora for my artwork...

740050428.text: A self-proclaimed collector came to you!? And they cited a high price, to boot... No wonder you said you didn't need Mora. If Paimon could sell her paintings for that much...

740050429.text: Hmm? Can you draw too, Paimon?

740050430.text: Err, not really. But maybe, with some hard work, starting today...

740051802.text: Are you alright? Are you hurt in any way?

740051803.text: I'm fine... But are you really people from that, uh, Maison Lumitoile place? You seem so strong...

740051804.text: #Oh, we were just trying to fool them! {NICKNAME} made that one up on the fly...

740051805.text: #But that did the trick, didn't it? {NICKNAME} does cut an upright and imposing figure — and Paimon's pretty cool and official-looking, right?

740051807.text: Standing straighter than your trusty Dull Blade!

740051809.text: And she'd be twice as cool if she wore the uniform!

740051901.text: They ran off, huh... Why do these people always need to take a beating before they'll cool off, huh?

740051902.text: But never mind that. Are you okay?

740051903.text: ...I'm fine. Thank you. I'm... not very good at dealing with such people.

740051905.text: Hehe. Well, we are well-honed professional adventurers, after all! People like that can't hold a candle to us, that's for sure!

740051906.text: #No... I don't mean {M#his}{F#her} skills. Anyway, {M#he}{F#she} was the only one fighting. You were just watching...

740051907.text: #Well, Paimon's a guide! We're just splitting the work, y'know. Right, {NICKNAME}?

740052001.text: I didn't expect to meet anyone else here. Are you here to gather inspiration, too?

740052003.text: This is a rather deserted place, but it is very beautiful. A painting that draws its inspiration from this place will surely be beloved.

740050503.text: Are you surprised, Paimon? And happy, that we have met again after all this while?

740050504.text: Well, it hasn't exactly been a "long while" since we last met... Actually, how did you get back sooner than us?

740050505.text: We didn't see you at all, either!

740050506.text: I came back immediately after packing, and I wound up waiting for you here.

740050507.text: Well, alright then. Also, is this Merusea Village? All the houses are kinda small — pretty interesting...

740050508.text: Maybe we've got a Melusine Chef, a Melusine Adventurer, or a Melusine Architect who specializes in building Melusine houses in this village! Hey, Mamere, what does your house look like?

740050509.text: My house is pretty and quiet. It's a good place to paint. Come on, it's this way.

740050101.text: Well. Um, this place is my house. Ahem! And, uh... Welcome to my humble abode. Please don't mind the mess and... all comments are welcome, and...

740050102.text: No need to be so formal! So, this place is a quiet spot suited for painting because it's a good distance from the village, huh...

740050104.text: *garbled mechanical noises* Welcome back, milady. You are as gentle, lovely, and radiant as ever.

740050105.text: Whoa! Did that robot dog just talk!?

740050106.text: #Yes! Paimon, {NICKNAME}, this is Seymour — he's family!

740050107.text: #Seymour, these two are {NICKNAME} and Paimon. They're nice people who stopped others from giving me Mora.

740050108.text: Don't phrase it like that! You make it sound like we did something bad...

740050109.text: Actually, never mind that. Why can Seymour speak?

740050110.text: What do you mean? Of course he can — there'd be something wrong with him if that wasn't the case!

740050113.text: #No, no! Stop simply agreeing with people, {NICKNAME}! No robot dog can talk, no matter where they're from!

740050116.text: Hmm... Since you're from abroad, I guess you know what you're talking about. That said, Seymour can talk, and he's also my best friend. He even critiques my paintings.

740050117.text: I see. Your judgment is very sharp, milady.

740050118.text: (It just talked again! Paimon's sure that Mamere isn't doing ventriloquism or anything... But does their exchange really make sense? It feels... mismatched.)

740050115.text: Is that so? But Seymour can.

740051401.text: Y'know, Paimon thinks we've seen this type of easel before.

740051402.text: Seems to be a design from outside the village...

740051403.text: Hmm. Speaking of that, how do the Melusines of Merusea Village trade with merchants from outside? Paimon doesn't think normal merchants would be any good at diving...

740051404.text: Hmm... Actually, this could be a great business opportunity for us, don't you think? If we took over all foreign trade for Merusea Village, we'd be rich!

740051406.text: Right? Hehe, that was a pretty good call from Paimon, huh? Let's explore the possibility later!

740052102.text: It's rude to go through other people's stuff, Paimon.

740052103.text: Hey, Paimon just happened to see it, alright?

740052104.text: But still... it seems like there's some machine components inside, though they're a bit...

740052105.text: Might these be tools used to maintain Seymour? Guess it might be best not to mess with them, then...

740051601.text: Y'know, Paimon's got a question. Why's Seymour the only clockwork mechanism that can talk?

740051603.text: Hmm. But if that's the case, why did it get left here?

740051604.text: You'd think that a new invention from the Fontaine Research Institute would...

740051605.text: Waaait a minute... Did the explosive accident at the Institute back then send Seymour flying all the way here?

740052601.text: Yes! I want to draw the most beautiful things.

740052602.text: #Common paints are fine, but they won't be able to portray the warmth that {NICKNAME} emanates or Paimon's shininess.

740052603.text: Give me a second. I'm gonna gather the paints I need.

740052605.text: Yeah, that's right. Your hands are so short — it might be tough for you to hold the paint bucket by yourself...

740052607.text: Also, there's no need to worry. I've always gone out to get paints on my own, so I'm used to it...

740052608.text: Wait, so you don't have friends accompanying you most of the time?

740052610.text: Oh! Uh... What Paimon means is... Um, sorry...

740052612.text: Oh, I get it, Paimon! You feel bad for me because Seymour can't move and I might be lonely while collecting paint, right? You're so nice... Thank you.

740052614.text: But anyway, we should go together. It'll be more convenient that way... right?

740052616.text: Hmm... If you're both willing, then let's go!

740052617.text: Thank you... That makes me so happy!

740052618.text: Hehe. Well, Paimon really does want to see your work, y'know!

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the place to collect the paint

740050701.text: #Look, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. Those are the ores that we need. Now, what we need to do next is...

740050702.text: Hehe! Say no more! We're expert miners! We'll show you how the pros do it!

740050707.text: U—Um, please wait. Digging directly isn't going to work...

subQuests.subQuestName: Use the prisms to resonate with the ore

740050801.text: (Battle) Looks like there's no reasoning with you.

740050802.text: Hah! You're the one who's disrupting a legitimate business transaction here!

740050803.text: Whatever, this is getting annoying. You two, with me! Let's get this kid!

740050804.text: What did I say? I knew things would come to this in the end...

740050901.text: So that's how we're doing this, huh...

740050902.text: But as long as we grind this ore into powder, we can make paints, right, Mamere?

740050903.text: Eh? Where's Mamere? She was here a moment ago...

740050905.text: Seriously. Someone that small shouldn't go running around like that... Never mind. Let's head up ahead too!

740050906.text: #Eh? {NICKNAME}? Are you okay? You're zoning out again...

740050907.text: Nothing. I'm just a bit dizzy.

740050908.text: Just like before...? Uh... Have you just not had enough to eat or something?

740050911.text: Don't push yourself too hard, alright? ...Let's keep going, shall we?

subQuests.subQuestName: Use the prisms to resonate with the ore again

740051201.text: Looks like we've already gathered loads of stuff. This should do it, right?

740051202.text: Wow! So much ore! I can make lots and lots of paints with these. Thank you so much!

740051203.text: Hehe, no need! But they're all red ore... Will you have enough colors to use?

740051204.text: Don't worry about it. Now, time for the last step!

740051205.text: Ooh, Paimon knows! You're gonna grind the ores and make them into paints! Is that right?

740051206.text: Huh? Hmm. Well, if you put it like that... Counting the need to grind the paints, there should be two more steps instead...

740051207.text: These ores contain a lot of impurities. If we were to make them into paint like this, the colors won't be even — they'll look dirty.

740051208.text: Huh. Paimon didn't know that there were so many considerations at play... Guess that's what makes you a master of the arts!

740051209.text: So, what do we do, Master Mamere?

740051210.text: Hehe. At this time, we need to find purer ores, grind them down, and then mix the powders together.

740051211.text: This way, the amount of impurities will decrease, and the paints we get from them will be more beautiful.

740051212.text: But shouldn't we have just used the purer ores to make the paints from the beginning?

740051213.text: There aren't that many high-purity ores around, silly! You might as well be saying that "If there's no Tidalga to eat, let's have Poissonchant Pie instead!"

740051214.text: Whoa, that metaphor sure gives you a distinct taste of Melusine food culture... That said, there aren't any other mineral veins nearby, are there?

740051215.text: Yes... We'll need to go further inside this place to find the purer ore we need.

740051216.text: Do you want to take a break? I can take care of the rest. I won't be long anyway!

740051217.text: We'll go with you... Wait. Look over there! Is that...

740051226.text: A red... whirlpool? Wormhole? What is that?

740051227.text: It's a shortcut. Haven't you seen one before? There should've been many of them along the way...

740051228.text: A shortcut? It looks pretty ominous for one... Is this what they call "a shortcut that's the longest way around"?

740051229.text: Well, I always take paths like these. They're safe. And warm.

740051230.text: Well, uh, if you say so then! We've come this far, so we might as well go all the way in helping you find high-purity ores!

740051302.text: E—Exactly! You know what happens to those who break the law here in Fontaine, don't you?

740051303.text: Don't take that tone with me! "What happens to those who break the law," my foot! Who do you think you are, anyway?

740051304.text: I'll say this one more time — stay out of this. This is between us and the kid!

740053001.text: Whoa... Paimon feels nauseous. This shortcut really was something. Was that... part of Melusine culture too?

740053002.text: On closer inspection, it seems like we did pass this place by when we came down. To think that there was such a large stone over there...

740053003.text: That's right, and this place feels warm and safe, doesn't it? Father told me about it, and it contains high-purity ores. I'll take care of the ones here, so just wait for me.

740053004.text: Uh, these don't look all that different from the ordinary sort...

740053005.text: Huh? But their colors are totally different...

740053006.text: R—Really? Aren't they all red anyway?

740053007.text: Well, yes, but there are pretty obvious differences between different shades of red, right?

740053009.text: I—It's fine. The differences are actually really small. It's normal that you're not able to tell the difference...

740053010.text: Wait, didn't you say they were obvious?

740053014.text: Still, you probably know a lot more about painting than we do, Mamere, and about ores and paints, too.

740053015.text: Either way, Paimon didn't know that painting was such tough work! Mining, gathering different ores to make paints... Paimon used to think that it was just about putting paint on canvas...

740053012.text: Hmm? You're really sensitive to colors... Would you like to paint someday? We can paint together. We'll put your paintings and mine together around the house!

740053013.text: ...You couldn't tell the difference at all, could you?

subQuests.subQuestName: Adjust the position of the prism to let it resonate with the ore
Adjust the position of the prism to let it resonate with the ore

740052401.text: Do you need to collect the paints yourself?

740053103.text: Hehe, we weren't just watching, y'know! We've also collected loads of "pure ore." Awesome, right?

740053105.text: Nice! Beautiful paints, here we come! Let's head back, shall we?

740053110.text: But you're right, I am very happy.

740053111.text: We can make lots of paint now.

740053112.text: Well, yes, that is part of it.

740053113.text: Oh? What about the other reasons, then?

740053114.text: Well, let's just head back first!

740053115.text: Hey! Paimon's talking to you, y'know!

740053117.text: #Ugh... Whatever. We'll need to get back to get that painting anyway, so let's just do that, {NICKNAME}!

740054601.text: Me? You can call me Jakob. I am a... traveling collector of art.

740054602.text: Good to see you again as well, Ms. Mamere.

740054604.text: So... Were all the things you told me lies?

740054605.text: That "you've never seen paintings like these before," that "you'd like to collect them"... That you could... understand them...

740054606.text: You did all that... for things that have nothing to do with the paintings themselves, right?

740054608.text: I have never intended to deceive you. Even now, I have nothing but admiration for your work.

740054610.text: And I apologize for my imprecise use of words. I was truly mesmerized by their unpredictable, chaotic nature, and I can appreciate the beauty in them, so incomprehensible to the rest of the world.

740054612.text: Of course I mean it. Your skills are most "enchanting," and your use of colors and persistence in making your own paints truly make me...

740054613.text: Hey! Don't be taken in by him so easily!

740054614.text: Uh... Wait, so this is a trick too...?

740054615.text: What do you want the paints for?

740054616.text: #...What an interesting question. A fine question indeed, {M#Sir}{F#Miss}.

740054617.text: Let me ask you this instead: what else do you think these paints can be used for?

740054618.text: Hmph. Paimon doesn't know what you wanna do with them, but you can't be up to anything good!

740054619.text: You tried to buy her paintings for a high price, and you also hired people to trouble her and ransack her house... You didn't have to go this far for your own drawings, did you?

740054620.text: Yes, why indeed? Consider that a question for further exploration after this discussion. For now, let me venture a guess: You have just collected the raw materials for the paints, am I correct?

740054621.text: #In that case, {M#sir}{F#ma'am}, allow me to ask you a question — could you give those materials to me?

740054622.text: I have no quarrel with you. As such, we need not be enemies.

740054623.text: In return, I can give you any amount of Mora — as long as it is within reason, of course.

740054625.text: Exactly! These paints aren't ours! You should be asking Mamere, shouldn't you?

740054626.text: Are you really hoping for an answer? Or are you simply probing about my attitude?

740054627.text: Regardless, I will answer honestly — you and I both know that Ms. Mamere will{RUBY#[S]cannot} not stop me from obtaining her paints, but that the same cannot be said for you.

740054628.text: I... I never said anything like that! I'm not listening to you, you liar!

740054629.text: Hush now. Say no more, Ms. Mamere.

740054630.text: #You will give me the correct answer, won't you, {M#sir}{F#ma'am}?

740054631.text: Of course we will — and that's a big fat "no"! Mamere put in so much effort to create something so beautiful, and yet you're treating her like... like this!

740054632.text: This is the answer the three of you have agreed on? Well then. Understood.

740054633.text: First, allow me to thank you for helping me collect these paints.

740054634.text: And well, though it disappoints me to say this, that will be all.

740054635.text: "That will be all"? First you ransack someone's house, and then you say all that stuff — and now you wanna run off?

740054636.text: You misunderstand. I said "that will be all," not "goodbye."

740054637.text: Ms. Irus, I'd like to change the original terms of our commission.

740054639.text: Get rid of these people. As for your pay... Will seven times the original amount do?

740054640.text: #Heh! You don't think you can take {NICKNAME} out with just these few people, do you?

740054641.text: Y—Y'know, boss, she's right. We won't be able to take that person out by ourselves...

740054642.text: You're mercenaries, aren't you? You should know more about combat than I do.

740054643.text: Since you have the numbers, why are you fixated on your strongest foe? Is there not someone there who cannot fight?

740054645.text: You mean you want us to...

740054646.text: What do you think you're doing?

740054647.text: Taking sensible, necessary action toward achieving a future far beyond our imaginations.

740054648.text: Tsk, seven-fold pay... There's no arguing, then. Sorry, buddy!

740054650.text: Please do not mind my appearance, milady. My prime directive is to... *garbled mechanical noises* protect you.

740054653.text: Affirmative. I am here, milady. You are as gentle, lovely, and radiant as ever.

740053501.text: Ahem. We heard it, too! But we don't know anything about clockwork meka, so... What should we do, exactly?

740053504.text: ...This is what I'm talking about. Pretty, isn't it?

740053505.text: This is... a scrap mechanical part?

740053506.text: Are they really scrap, though? They're so shiny and pretty, and they're everywhere here. Everyone in the village really likes them, and so they all have some...

740053507.text: When we help each other out, we give the other components as tokens of gratitude. And Xana likes them more than most, so she often exchanges a lot of nice things for them. Oh, but she doesn't seem to be in the village...

740053508.text: So they're currency specific to Merusea Village?

740053513.text: Currency? Oh. I get it. Like Mora! Well, I guess you can say that. Hmm... Even if Jakob were to give me a lot of components in exchange for my paintings, I wouldn't accept... unless it would help me fix Seymour...

740053514.text: Alright, sure. We just need to collect components, right? We'll help!

740053515.text: No way! They're like Mora, you know. Getting parts for me would be like me asking you to, um... earn Mora for me? That sounds like something a villain would do!

740053519.text: I'll also go hunt them down myself. I really can't ask you to find them for me while I just sit around doing nothing!

740051001.text: Hmm. It seems that I must now reveal my true identity...

740051003.text: I'm an enforcer of the law.

740051005.text: Oh, yeah, that's right! You've got a good eye, huh?

740051006.text: W—Wait, Sis, what do we do...

740051007.text: #Wh—What are you worried about? If {M#he's}{F#she's} a law enforcer, I'm the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya! You're just gonna believe everything people say, are you?

740051008.text: And just look at them! Do they look like folks from the, uh, Mai... Mais...

740051010.text: That's right, that's the one. Seriously, what's with the ridiculous name? They're just law enforcement, so they might as well call themselves that!

740051011.text: Anyway, you think we've never seen people from the Maison before? You aren't even in uniform — daring impostors, aren't you?

740050203.text: Hmph! Whatever. Not that there's anything more to talk about, anyway. Let's just take the stuff and go!

740050205.text: C—C'mon, little one, no need to make that face.

740050206.text: *sigh* Why did we take this job again? Whatever...

740050207.text: Hey, Kaykubad! What are you doing just watching over there? Just toss her the boss's Mora — then let's take the paintings and go!

740050208.text: Eh, do we have to, though? He doesn't know what we're doing this far out. Why don't we just take the Mora and...

740050209.text: How do they put it again? Favors are more important to deals than Mora...

740050210.text: Hey, what are you guys doing?

740050211.text: Wha... Where did you pop out from?

740050212.text: Looks like you're bothering this young lady.

740050213.text: Her? Bothered? We're just here to buy some artwork, you know...

740050214.text: Buying? How much were you gonna pay for one?

740050216.text: Wait, you don't have any hard figures at all!

740050217.text: Well, that's not our fault — this Melusine won't talk!

740050218.text: Well, if she doesn't wanna talk to you, then she doesn't wanna sell! You're just here to take her stuff, aren't you?

740050219.text: Take!? This is a fair exchange, a fair and square exchange! We're not gonna short-change her... And what's this to you, anyway?

740050221.text: Nonsense! Paimon heard that guy over there talking about taking the Mora—

740050222.text: Tch! Told you to watch your mouth, you...!

740050223.text: Does it really matter? Haven't we always solved things this way up till now?

740050224.text: Can't you ever shut up? We don't have the time to involve unrelated people! Besides—

740050226.text: Nothing! Buzz off, you're butting into legitimate business here!

740050227.text: If not, I'm afraid we might have to resort to less... savory methods to settle this.

740050601.text: Eh? What's this small bottle for?

740050602.text: Only one way to find out.

740050603.text: Huh. This looks like... paint? There's only a little left, but still...

740050608.text: Why don't we sit down and take a break here first? You might be tired from all that swimming...

740050610.text: That's good... But don't push yourself, alright? If you feel sick later, just say so!

740050612.text: Ah, Mamere. Are your painting tools ready?

740050613.text: Um, uh... Again, welcome to my humble abode. Please don't mind the mess and... all comments are welcome...

740050614.text: But, um... I think... I'm out of paints...

740050616.text: I mean the stuff that should've been in that bottle... a warm and beautiful color...

740050617.text: Anyway, sorry, but please wait here a moment. I'll go to gather some paints — I'll be right back...

740050618.text: No need to apologize! A priceless masterpiece like the one you'll make should also need priceless paints, after all!

740050607.text: Wh—What? A white fish? Are you sure you're okay?

740051501.text: Alain's little invention... Might as well have been yesterday since I last saw it.

740051503.text: We searched her place, but we couldn't find the paints you wanted...

740051505.text: Y—Yes. We did find some bottles that once contained paints, though. They gave off a very pungent smell that made us feel all queasy...

740051506.text: I see, so the paints have been used up. Well, that's an unfortunate coincidence.

740051507.text: Well then, Ms. Irus, please take your people and clean this place up — as things stand, this would make for too shocking a sight, I think.

740051508.text: As for the "paints"... I'll figure something out later.

740051510.text: Um... Sorry, sir. We couldn't complete your commission. Before you could personally come to that little squirt's aid, those two strangers came and stole the moment...

740051511.text: It's fine. I'm not bothered by this.

740051512.text: Well, it's not so much about that... But don't you think that this would count as a case of force majeure, as such? So, um, about the remuneration we discussed previously...

740051514.text: Don't worry. You will be paid as per usual.

740051515.text: R—Really? Thank you, sir! Ah, if only all our employers were as good-hearted as you!

740051516.text: Whatever the case, I shan't take up any more of your time — just clean these shambolic doodles up.

740051519.text: Aaand what are you doing here?

740051520.text: Hey, purple guy! Are you in cahoots with those thieves who wanted to steal Mamere's paintings? ... Oh, Paimon knows what you're up to, alright!

740051521.text: You hired these people to steal Mamere's artwork to create an opportunity for you to rescue her, win her trust, and then achieve some unspeakable aims...

740051522.text: Well, not that Paimon thinks getting paints counts as anything unspeakable, but...

740051523.text: #Eavesdropping is a bad habit, {M#good sir, good lady}{F#good ladies}.

740051524.text: And you're one to talk! Coming here on the sly and ransacking someone's house when they're not in — you've got some cheek to call others out!

740051704.text: Alain's "own little invention." You've been slumbering for years, haven't you?

740051706.text: Yeah, just stop plotting all this bad stuff! Why are you so obsessed with these paints, anyway? Are they really worth you resorting to such despicable actions...?

740051707.text: Please. I've already told you why "we" are doing this.

740051708.text: As for you, Ms. Mamere, if we should meet again... I look forward to your future drawings.

740051711.text: #Well then, I'll take my leave, {M#good sir and ladies}{F#good ladies}. Ah yes, and you, thinking machine. Let's go, Ms. Irus. We have other things to do.

740051712.text: Hey! Stop right there, Purple Guy!

740051713.text: P—Please wait, you two! There's... There's something wrong with Seymour.

740051718.text: Out of energy... So you mean...

740051722.text: Oh, Seymour... Mr. Jakob... He always intended to trick me by saying all those things like "I love your paintings," "I can understand your paintings"...

740051723.text: And even worse... He damaged you this badly... I won't forgive him... I won't! *sobs*

740051724.text: Mamere, let's go look for an engineer in the Court of Fontaine. They should be able to fix or even improve upon him, and we can also help you find more paints along the way!

740051725.text: But let's pack things up a bit first. Oh, Paimon hopes your paintings weren't damaged during the fight.

740051727.text: It's just... What's the point of all my old work? If Seymour can't be cured... If Seymour can't appraise these works like he used to...

740051730.text: Artworks that no one understands... Those aren't really artworks, are they? They're just what that person called them — "shambolic doodles."

740051731.text: Don't say that! Even that Purple Guy said that there was something magical and "inscrutably disordered" about your work. Paimon loves your stuff too!

740051733.text: Also, Paimon's wanted to ask about this since before. What do you mean by everyone in the village "not understanding art"?

740051734.text: Exactly that. No one understands the paintings.

740051735.text: Bah! They only don't get it because they don't have your artistic background, so they can't get the... uh... hidden meanings! Well, everything's about context anyway, right? That means you'll need societal knowledge and an understanding of history...

740051736.text: Uhm... What Paimon wants to say is... Can we see the paintings?

740051738.text: You pick a painting up from the ground...

740051740.text: (Paimon doesn't really understand its contents either, but it looks really awesome... and this might sound unsuitable, but it looks like it might be super valuable right off the bat...)

740051741.text: It's... so beautiful! For example... Uh, these details here, they've really got that... immersive feeling. D—Don't you think so too? The other Melusines probably don't understand it because...

740051742.text: You don't have to force yourself to say something nice, Paimon. I can see right through you.

740051743.text: Still, I know you're doing this out of the goodness of your heart, so, thank you.

740051744.text: Um, sorry... Paimon couldn't tell what you'd painted, but... it really is very beautiful.

740051745.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's help pack this stuff up...

740052501.text: I do recall us helping Albedo gather Starsilver back then...

740052502.text: That's true... But the ore that we picked up then didn't really get put to any use, did they?

740053401.text: Thank you. Sorry, I made you clean up after me again. Y'know, just like when we met for the first time?

740053402.text: It's fine. We're friends, after all!

740053404.text: Looks like you're in a good mood again. That's great!

740053405.text: Yeah. I feel so happy when I'm with you guys, just like how I feel when I'm on a roll with my paintings.

740053406.text: Still, looking at how you're packing things up, Paimon can't help but think that you Melusines really have short hands...

740053407.text: Hmph! Your hands are even shorter, Paimon!

740053411.text: Alright, alright! Paimon takes it back. But, really, don't those hands make painting inconvenient? Your canvas does sit on a high stand...

740053412.text: It's alright, since my hands aren't short at all! But... speaking of painting, I really am sorry that I won't be able to paint for you at the moment.

740053413.text: I just... can't leave Seymour like this. I must fix him first — he is my best friend, after all.

740053415.text: Sorry, Paimon. But I'll paint for you once Seymour's all fixed up.

740053416.text: Right! Let's go to the Court of Fontaine together and seek out a reliable engineer to help us!

740053417.text: An engineer...? No, that's not it... I want to fix Seymour myself.

740053418.text: Huh? Wait. You know how to fix clockwork meka, too?

740053421.text: Strange that you would even ask, Paimon. Of course not.

740053425.text: But, how are you gonna fix him, then?

740053426.text: Father said that he's seen a lot of machines, both intact and dismantled, so he can teach me how to fix Seymour.

740053428.text: Hmm... You've mentioned this "Father" a few times previously. What's he like? A master Melusine engineer with a long mustache? A Melusine with a wrench?

740053431.text: Huh? U—Uh, did Paimon say something bad? Why'd you stop talking...

740053434.text: W—Wait a moment. Who are you talking to?

740053435.text: Are... the ones I have at home not enough? Then...

740053439.text: Whoa! Wait, you're talking to us again!

740053440.text: Father has told me how to cure Seymour. We just need to collect enough components, and...

740053441.text: Come on, don't worry! I'll paint for you once Seymour is all fixed up.

740053442.text: No! We're not worried about the painting! Ugh... Who were you talking to just now?

740053445.text: Um... Uh, Father is Father? Wait... Can the two of you not hear Father's voice?

740053446.text: The voice, you say... Oh, yeah, of course we did!

740053447.text: (Uh... Has Seymour's breakdown hit her too hard or something? Anyway, let's just go along with this for now! We can comfort her later...)

740054501.text: I believe we've met before, yes?

740054502.text: #Commendable memory you have, {M#sir}{F#ma'am}. Yes, we did have the honor of meeting near a cliff before you made a mess of my plans.

740054503.text: It's just that, at the time, I didn't think that you would make the same choice as me and help Ms. Mamere.

740054504.text: Don't lump what we did in with your little one-man-show!

740055001.text: Hmph. I'll have you know that this *is* the uniform of the Maison Lumitoile!

740055003.text: (Hang on a second, what in the world is that!? Who even calls themselves that?)

740055004.text: Pfft. To think that outlanders these days no longer recognize the uniform of the Maison Lumitoile...

740055005.text: Wh—What? But what kind of ridiculous name is that? Is this some out-of-season joke?

740055006.text: Irus, I'd be careful... If nothing else, this person's confidence is not faked.

740055007.text: Besides, think about it — do you really think someone who was trying to trick us would use such an obviously nonsensical name?

740055008.text: You say that, but even so, I doubt anyone would name their department that...

740055009.text: Exactly! Why would anyone— Uh, how dare you call our name nonsensical? Paimon's not gonna take this lying down!

740055010.text: #Officer {NICKNAME}, inform these ignorant outlanders of our organization's glorious history!

740055012.text: (Who chose to protect everyone regardless of the means used... Hang on a minute, does Paimon know this person too?)

740055013.text: A—Anyway, that mighty, invincible hero was like a Lumitoile illuminating the night, showing others the way forward!

740055014.text: And that is why we call ourselves the Maison Lumitoile in his honor!

740055019.text: So, hmph! How dare you call our name weird!?

740055021.text: Hey! What are you apologizing for?

740055022.text: #Well, boss, if you look a little closer, {M#his cape and her clothes}{F#their clothes} not only match, but are actually very unique...

740055024.text: Aren't... they just the same color? Do you think some clothes and some words are enough for people to pose as officials?

740055017.text: A—Anyway, our founder did battle against those monsters and, like a Lumitoile, lit the seas up once more!

740055018.text: And that is why we call ourselves the Maison Lumitoile in his honor!

740055101.text: Take this new-model Gardemek, for instance.

740055102.text: (Hey! What in the world's a Gardemek, huh?)

740055105.text: (Wait a minute! This story is getting crazier by the second!)

740055106.text: I see. I get it now...

740055107.text: Wh—What do you mean you "get it"?

740055108.text: I've heard it said in the taverns that someone saw meka that are more like humans... This could be the equipment this Maison Lumitoile member is using.

740055110.text: *cough* That is correct. Paimon's prime directives are to serve the public, protect the citizenry, and uphold the law...

740055111.text: According to... the Pumpkin Protocol, those who take advantage of others must not be let off lightly...

740055112.text: P-Type Gardemek. Load and charge your kinetic cannon.

740055113.text: Beep... beep.. boop... Charging complete. Target locked. Um... Jellenergy Cannon activating...

740055114.text: W—Wait! What in the world is that? What are you doing?

740055201.text: Don't you know the face of Fontaine's General Mahamatra?

740055202.text: Ack! The General Mahamatra!? It's game over for us! Game over!

740055203.text: Calm down, you bone-headed numbskull! Why would the General Mahamatra be here, huh?

740055204.text: Um, uh, this is a new post based on Sumeru's system...

740055205.text: (N—No, that's not gonna fly, is it? Why did you have to mention the Mahamatra!?)

740055206.text: Enough! Enough nonsense! If you're intent on stopping us, then we'll just have to show you what for! You two, with me!

740055207.text: What did I say? I knew things would come to this in the end...

740055302.text: Plainclothes, you say? What do we look like to you, gullible kids?

740055303.text: Well, I'd call this less "not being gullible" and more "knowing what to look out for from experience" — weren't you the one who fell afoul of not one, or two, but several plainclothes police, to the point where you nearly got sent to court?

740055305.text: A—Anyway, if you really were plainclothes police, you'd know better than us that you need evidence before you can enforce the law, right?

740055307.text: Alright, that's it, cut the crap!

740055308.text: If you're intent on stopping us, then we'll just have to show you what for! You two, with me!

740055309.text: What did I say? I knew things would come to this in the end...

740055401.text: We're enforcers of the Corps of Thirty.

740055402.text: Eek! It's the Corps of Thirty!? Why are they here?

740055403.text: Hey, you idiot, calm yourself! Why *would* they be here, huh?

740055404.text: We're the, uh, the Fontaine branch of the Corps!

740055405.text: Seriously? Who do you think the Corps of Thirty are, anyway? Mints that grow in both Sumeru and Fontaine?

740055406.text: Uh, they could always be Sweet Flowers instead...

740055408.text: Or the Adventurers' Guild, or Katheryne...

740055409.text: Enough! Enough nonsense! If you're intent on stopping us, then we'll just have to show you what for! You two, with me!

740055410.text: What did I say? I knew things would come to this in the end...

740055501.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, could you wait for me in the village? I'll need to pack my painting tools before heading down there...
